title: Partial algebraization of a complete normal strictly local scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a normal complete strictly henselian local Noetherian excellent scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq2$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Complete means complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; normal means its local rings are integrally closed domains. There exist a finite surjective morphism $p:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with $X\prime$ normal, a complete regular local Noetherian excellent scheme $S$ of dimension $d-1$ with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], a finite-type morphism $Z\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a geometric point $\bar z\to Z$, such that $$X\prime\cong\widehat{Z_{(\bar z)}}.$$ Here $Z_{(\bar z)}$ is strict localization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and the hat is completion for its maximal ideal. The scheme $Z_{(\bar z)}$ is Noetherian excellent, admits a dimension function, and the completion map $X\prime\to Z_{(\bar z)}$ is regular (flat with geometrically regular fibres). In equal characteristic the finite cover may be taken to be the identity. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].
